assumptions: psi is a normalized vector in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
variables: rho: density operator; psi: unit state vector; bra is the adjoint of ket.
patches.regime: Rank-one orthogonal projector; rho squared equals rho. A mixed state is not represented by one such projector.

assumptions: p_i are nonnegative and sum to one; each psi_i has unit norm; finite ensemble in a finite-dimensional space.
variables: p_i: classical preparation probabilities; psi_i: normalized ensemble states, not necessarily orthogonal.
patches.regime: Ensemble decompositions are nonunique. The displayed sum may also be pure if all occupied vectors represent the same ray; having several terms alone does not imply mixedness.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.3.1 Eq. (2.60), p. 18 (spectral ensemble); Sec. 2.5.2 Eq. (2.98) and following discussion, pp. 28–30 (general nonunique ensembles).

assumptions: rho is positive semidefinite with trace one on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space of dimension d.
variables: gamma: purity; Tr: operator trace; d: Hilbert-space dimension.
patches.regime: 1/d <= gamma <= 1. Equality at one characterizes pure states; the minimum is attained by I/d. Purity is not a thermodynamic entropy.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.3.1, p. 18, discussion following Eq. (2.60): Tr(rho squared) equals the sum of squared eigenvalues. The finite-dimension lower bound follows by Cauchy–Schwarz.

assumptions: One qubit: rho is a positive trace-one 2 by 2 matrix.
variables: r: real three-component Bloch vector; sigma: standard Pauli matrices with eigenvalues plus/minus one; I: 2 by 2 identity.
patches.regime: The full state space is the closed Bloch ball, not just its boundary. |r|=1 gives pure states; |r|<1 gives mixed states. This parametrization does not describe arbitrary higher-dimensional states.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.3.2, Eq. (2.62) and positivity/pure-state discussion, printed/PDF p. 19; source P is renamed r.

assumptions: Normalized pure state of a finite-dimensional bipartite tensor-product Hilbert space.
variables: lambda_i: nonnegative eigenvalues of either reduced density matrix, summing to one; sqrt(lambda_i): Schmidt coefficients; i_A and i_B: paired orthonormal vectors.
patches.regime: Only nonzero terms need be retained. Degeneracies allow nonunique Schmidt bases; this is not a generic decomposition of mixed states or a simultaneous Schmidt decomposition of three subsystems.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.4, Eqs. (2.83)–(2.89), pp. 23–24; Eq. (2.88) is the displayed decomposition with p_i renamed lambda_i. Degeneracy discussion pp. 24–25.

assumptions: rho is a positive trace-one density operator in finite dimension; logarithm is defined spectrally with 0 log 0 interpreted as zero.
variables: S: von Neumann entropy; log: logarithm of the density operator.
patches.units: Base-2 logarithm gives bits; natural logarithm gives nats. No Boltzmann constant is included.
patches.regime: Entropy vanishes for pure states and is at most log(d). This expression alone is not a claim of thermal equilibrium or a thermodynamic entropy in joules per kelvin.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 10.2, Eqs. (10.59)–(10.62), printed p. 14 / PDF p. 20; logarithm base-2 convention at printed p. 3 / PDF p. 9.

assumptions: Normalized bipartite pure state; finite-dimensional tensor-product subsystems; rho_A is obtained by tracing over B.
variables: S_A: entropy of reduced state rho_A; Tr_B: partial trace over B.
patches.units: Base-2 logarithms give bits (ebits for pure-state entanglement); natural logarithms give nats.
patches.regime: For pure AB, S_A=S_B quantifies bipartite entanglement. For a mixed joint state the marginal entropy alone is not an entanglement measure; classical mixing can make it nonzero.

assumptions: rho and sigma are positive trace-one density operators on the same finite-dimensional Hilbert space; square roots are positive operator square roots.
variables: F: squared fidelity used here; Tr: trace; rho and sigma: states being compared.
patches.regime: This record uses squared fidelity. Watrous uses root fidelity f, so the displayed F=f squared; his Eq. (3.65) is squared after exchanging its symmetric arguments. For pure states this gives squared overlap. Do not interchange root and squared conventions in bounds.

assumptions: rho and sigma are density operators on the same finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
variables: D: half trace-norm distance; ||X||_1=Tr sqrt(X dagger X).
patches.regime: For equal prior probabilities, optimal single-copy discrimination succeeds with probability (1+D)/2. Watrous calls the full norm trace distance; the app deliberately retains the common half-norm convention.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional completely positive linear map; for a deterministic quantum channel require sum K_k dagger K_k = I.
variables: E: map on operators; K_k: Kraus operators from input to output Hilbert space; dagger: adjoint.
patches.units: Dimensionless map and Kraus operators for normalized finite-system states.
patches.regime: The sum establishes complete positivity, not trace preservation by itself. Kraus representations are nonunique. A selected measurement outcome is generally trace-decreasing and needs probability normalization for its conditional state.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 3.2.1, Eqs. (3.68)–(3.70), printed/PDF p. 17; finite-system operator sum and completeness.
Corollary 2.27, Eq. (2.129), printed p. 89 / PDF p. 97: finite-dimensional channel characterization including differing input/output spaces.

assumptions: K_k is a Kraus family for a completely positive linear map in finite dimension; equality is on the input space.
variables: K_k: input-to-output operators; I: identity on the input Hilbert space.
patches.regime: Equivalent to trace preservation for the operator-sum map. A probabilistic operation instead permits sum K_k dagger K_k <= I. Do not confuse this condition with unitality, which concerns sum K_k K_k dagger.

sourceLocations.locator: Corollary 2.27, Eq. (2.129), printed p. 89 / PDF p. 97, channel criterion.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional channel E from input A to output B; a fixed orthonormal basis on A and its reference copy R is chosen.
variables: Phi=sum_i |i>_R tensor |i>_A is UNNORMALIZED; J_E acts on R tensor B; I is the identity superoperator on R; d_A is input dimension.
patches.units: Dimensionless; for a trace-preserving channel Tr J_E=d_A, not one.
patches.regime: With this convention J_E is positive and Tr_B J_E=I_R. Using a unit-normalized Phi instead divides J_E and its partial trace by d_A. Watrous orders output before reference; the app orders reference before output, related by a tensor-factor swap.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.2.2, Eqs. (2.64)–(2.66), printed p. 78 / PDF p. 86 (unnormalized vec(I), output-first); Corollary 2.27, printed p. 89 / PDF p. 97 (positivity and trace condition). Explicit swap to reference-first ordering.
